content.title: Aerosol composition modulates diurnal and vertical contrasts of Beijing's urban heat island in winter haze
content.abstract: Abstract. Aerosols modify the surface radiation budget and boundary-layer heat exchange, thereby altering urban heat islands. Such radiative and thermal processes depend strongly on aerosol composition and differ between urban and rural environments, leading to height-dependent net effects. This vertical differentiation is critical for understanding thermal and dynamical controls on heat retention and pollutant accumulation during winter haze.
